note: Every use of a durability primitive outside crates/permguard-host/src/storage/ (WP-1.11): exact file, enclosing item, primitive and why the library cannot be used there. crates/permguard-conformance/tests/durability.rs keeps this list equal to the code: a use not listed fails, and so does an entry nothing needs. One entry covers every use of that primitive in that item.

allowed.reason: `replay.new`, the replay journal's compaction directory: a name, not a publication; the directory is created and swapped into place through `Dir`
recognises the `*.tmp` temporaries of the mirror layout before the library, to sweep them; nothing is published under the name
recognises the `*.tmp` temporaries of the object store layout before the library, to sweep them; nothing is published under the name

`SYNCED`, the mirror's freshness marker: its modification time is the datum and its content is empty, so an in-place write is the cheapest way to move the time and a torn one cannot exist (owner decision of 2026-10-07)
writes `5` to `/proc/<pid>/clear_refs` to reset the measured server's peak resident set before a benchmark step: a kernel control file, not stored data
the release benchmark's storage probe (TS-3): it measures what a data flush costs on the volume's storage, so it must call the flush itself; the probe file is scratch, removed after
copies the example workspace into the benchmark's scratch directory before the CLI applies it, so the repository's copy is never written: scratch input, not stored data
the configuration file of a server the benchmark starts in its own scratch directory: test input, written before the process that reads it exists
writes the benchmark report the run produced to the path its operator named: an output file of a tool, not Host state
